content: Melvin-Koushki first gives the straightforward reading: lettrists such as Ibn Turka preside over the rest of the hierarchy from level six but cannot reach level seven, which is reserved for the Imams in a gesture of deference, so that the schema would seem unremarkable apart from its Shiʿi and lettrist slant. He then says that on closer examination the seventh level is not entirely what it seems.
refers_to_primary: Ibn Turka, R. Shaqq-i Qamar u Bayān-i Sāʿat
